title: Hadith and Sunnah
lines: USAT questions on hadith ask what hadith and Sunnah mean, how a hadith is built and graded, who compiled the major collections, and what well-known hadith teach. Learn the terms and the compilers carefully; the teachings are best remembered by their meaning.
## Key terms
| Term | Meaning
| Hadith | a report of what the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said, did or approved
| Sunnah | the way or practice of the Prophet (PBUH); the second source of Islamic guidance after the Quran
| Qawli, fi'li, taqriri | saying, action, and silent approval (taqrir)
| Isnad (sanad) | the chain of narrators
| Matn | the text or content of the report
| Rawi | a narrator
| Sahabi | a companion who met the Prophet (PBUH) as a believer
| Tabi'i | a successor who met a companion
| Hadith Qudsi | a report in which the Prophet (PBUH) relates a meaning from Allah, in his own words
## Grades of hadith
- Sahih: sound. Every narrator is trustworthy with a strong memory, the chain is unbroken, and there is no hidden defect.
- Hasan: good. Like sahih but a narrator's memory is slightly less strong.
- Da'if: weak. A condition of acceptance is missing.
- Mawdu': fabricated, falsely attributed to the Prophet (PBUH), and rejected.
## Why hadith matter

The Quran commands Muslims to obey the Messenger (PBUH), and the Sunnah explains how its commands are carried out. For example, the Quran orders prayer and zakat; the Sunnah shows the number of rakats, the timings and the rates. Hadith also record the Prophet's (PBUH) character, which the Quran calls the best example.
## The six well-known collections
| Collection | Compiler | Note
| Sahih al-Bukhari | Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari | regarded as the most authentic book after the Quran
| Sahih Muslim | Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj | with Bukhari, called the Sahihayn
| Sunan Abu Dawud | Imam Abu Dawud | focus on legal hadith
| Jami' at-Tirmidhi | Imam at-Tirmidhi | notes the grade of many hadith
| Sunan an-Nasa'i | Imam an-Nasa'i | known for strict standards
| Sunan Ibn Majah | Imam Ibn Majah | completes the six

Other well-known works: the Muwatta of Imam Malik, an early collection from Madinah; the Musnad of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, arranged by companion; and the Forty Hadith (Al-Arba'in) of Imam an-Nawawi, a short collection of core teachings. Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrated the largest number of hadith; Aisha (RA) is among the leading narrators.
## Collection in stages
- In the Prophet's (PBUH) time, companions memorised his words, and some wrote them down.
- Later generations travelled widely to hear hadith from those who had heard them, and recorded each chain of narrators.
- In the third century after the Hijrah, the great collections such as Bukhari and Muslim were completed, with careful checking of every chain.
## Well-known teachings (by meaning)
- Actions are judged by intentions. This hadith opens Sahih al-Bukhari.
- The strong person is not the one who wrestles others down, but the one who controls himself when angry.
- Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or keep silent.
- None of you truly believes until he wants for his brother what he wants for himself.
- A kind word is charity, and removing something harmful from the road is a branch of faith.
- The signs of a hypocrite include lying when speaking, breaking promises and betraying trust.
- Make things easy and do not make them difficult.
> A companion did something in front of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who saw it and did not object. This kind of Sunnah is called
> (A) qawli  (B) fi'li  (C) taqriri  (D) qudsi
> C. Taqrir is silent approval. Qawli is a saying and fi'li an action of the Prophet (PBUH) himself; qudsi refers to a report of Allah's words.
> The chain of narrators of a hadith is called the  (A) matn  (B) isnad  (C) rawi  (D) sahih
> B. The matn is the text, a rawi is one narrator, and sahih is a grade.
## Traps
! Do not mix isnad and matn: the isnad comes first and lists the people; the matn is what was said.
! A Hadith Qudsi is not part of the Quran, although its meaning is from Allah.
! The Muwatta is by Imam Malik and the Musnad by Imam Ahmad; neither is one of the six.
## Quick check
- Hadith: saying, action or approval of the Prophet (PBUH).
- Isnad = chain; matn = text; grades sahih, hasan, da'if, mawdu'.
- Sahihayn = Bukhari and Muslim; then Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah.
- Most hadith narrated by Abu Hurayrah (RA).
